newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on closed-end fund selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on closed-end fund selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices reversed early gains to close slightly lower on Thursday on late selling by closed-end funds which were facing pressure to convert into open-end funds, brokers said.

"Several closed-end funds are approaching their conversion levels, so they sold electronics and financials to lower their net asset value to reduce the conversion pressure," said Tank Hung of Yuanta Securities.
The index ended down 29.76 points or 0.46 percent at 6,425.68, down from an opening high of 6,476.71.
Turnover was an active T$47.67 billion.

Under Taiwan's rules, closed-end fund investors can request to convert the funds into open-end funds if the fund's market price shows a 20 percent discount campared with its net asset value for over 20 straight sessions.
Electronics recorded the sharpest loss, with Acer down T$1.7 to T$38.7 and Mitac down 90 cents to T$23.8.
Paper, construction and financial shares also fell.
But textiles rose slightly on rising order hope and recent product price hikes, with Far Eastern Textile up 60 cents to T$31.1 and Shinkong Synthetic Fibre up 10 cents to T$23.3.
The index remained higher during most of the session, boosted by increasing inflows of foreign funds since August.

The central bank said on Wednesday that foreign funds showed a net inflow in August and early September, against July's net outflows, and foreign funds can put US$38.86 billion more into Taiwan's stock market before hitting an official ceiling.

For Friday, a consolidation between 6,380 and 6,450 was seen. But brokers noted optimistic prospects afterwards. "I don't expect bad news in the near term except for U.S.-Iraq conflicts. After a short consolidation, the index should rise again to test 6,500," Hung said. -- James Peng (5080815)
